subject: urban-planning
intro: Urban planning leads to the work of deciding how cities grow — zoning and transport, housing and climate resilience — plus the mapping, engineering and design professions that turn plans into places.

roles.title: Urban and Regional Planners
roles.what: Shape how places grow: draft comprehensive plans, write and administer zoning codes, review development proposals, run community engagement, and advise councils on land use, transport, housing and the environment.
roles.where: Nearly the whole syllabus is the job description — land use and the comprehensive plan, zoning law, transportation, housing and community development, and the GIS and scenario methods of unit 8.

roles.title: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
roles.what: Make and maintain the maps underneath modern decisions: gather data from aerial images, satellites and field survey, build geographic information system layers, and produce the map products planners and engineers rely on.
roles.where: Unit 8's GIS-for-planning and demographic analysis topics, plus the aerial and satellite imagery content of the survey unit, are the exact data craft this role is paid for.

roles.title: Landscape Architects
roles.entry: Bachelor's or master's degree in landscape architecture
roles.what: Design outdoor space: plan parks, plazas, streetscapes and campuses, choose planting and materials, handle grading and drainage, and develop green infrastructure that manages stormwater and heat.
roles.where: Unit 6's urban design and placemaking, streets and public space, and unit 7's green infrastructure and climate adaptation topics are this role's design brief.

roles.title: Surveyors
roles.what: Measure the land precisely: establish official boundaries, take positions for deeds and construction, record terrain for maps and subdivision design, and certify where property lines and easements actually fall.
roles.where: The subdivision and development-control topics of the planning law unit, and the land-use classification and parcel thinking of unit 2, sit directly on the boundary evidence surveyors produce.

roles.title: Civil Engineers
roles.what: Build the physical city: design roads, transit lines, water systems and drainage, run the studies and models behind them, and make sure what is constructed meets codes, budgets and environmental review.
roles.where: The transportation planning unit — travel demand, mode choice, transit and induced demand — plus environmental review and hazard mitigation give planners' engineering counterparts their shared language.
